newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Friday, with scattered bids at $67.00 per cwt passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00, feedlot sources said.
The bids were unchanged from late sales on Thursday at $67.00 in Kansas, which were down $1.00 from active trades on Wednesday and down $2.00 from brisk movement last week.
Fed cattle prices slipped this week amid weaker beef prices, which were attributed to hefty cattle kills.
The lower prices also attracted increased buying from retailers for Memorial Day holiday weekend featuring.

Beef prices on Thursday were quoted down $0.02 to $0.42 per cwt, with 299 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was down $0.02 at $106.07, compared with Wednesday and down $0.90 since last Friday.
Beef sales for the week to date on Thursday were 1,191 fabricated loads, up 23.9 percent from the previous week at 961, the USDA statistics showed.

Several feedlot sources said uncertainty over Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report could keep activity light. The report is expected to show on-feed supplies May 1 near 10 percent over last year and active April placements.
